userStories.title: AGENT kind and dispatch shape
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the AGENT kind and its additive protocol/dispatch input shape while preserving existing commands.

**Motivation** — koda has no job that runs an arbitrary agent task and returns its text: `REVIEW` and `FIX` post to a PR, `PLAN` and `RUN` produce a PRD or a branch, and config jobs run no agent.

**Approach** — Verbatim design: **Input shape.** The dispatch body gains `agent: { name, task, model?, modelAliases?, timeoutSec? }`, stored on the job as one JSON column `agentInput`. `feature` stays required and follows the existing feature rules, so the existing one-active-job-per-`(repoId, feature)` rule applies to `AGENT` too. `ref` defaults to the repo's default branch as for `RUN` and `PLAN`. `NewFleetJob.agentInput` is optional (absent means null), so the config-job and thread job builders need no change.

**Raw bash only, no tickets.** `AGENT` requires `bashMode` `raw` (an unattended agent denies every ask, so a relay adds nothing; the runner's assign parser enforces it too) and refuses `ticketRefs`, `planFrom` and `prNumber`.

Add AGENT to FleetJobKind, the FleetJobDto command enum, protocol FleetJobKindName and the exhaustive kinds record in protocol.spec.ts. Add the optional nested DispatchAgentDto and agentInput:null to all non-AGENT normalizeDispatch results, updating existing whole-object test expectations. Reject a missing agent with ValidationAppException({ reason: 'agent required for AGENT' }, 'fleet.dispatchInput'), agent on another kind with 'agent is only for AGENT', non-raw bash with 'bashMode must be raw for AGENT', ticketRefs with 'ticketRefs is not for AGENT', planFrom with 'planFrom is only for PLAN', and prNumber with 'prNumber is only for REVIEW and FIX'. Store only the supplied input keys, without execution defaults. Create API structural types and the protocol runtime result limits; API production code must not import those limits as runtime values. Protocol RunnerCapabilities gains agentsRun?:true; SnapshotEventPayload gains agentResult?:AgentJobResult; AssignPayload gains agent?:AgentAssign.

**Scope** — In: kind/DTO/protocol shape, command-specific exclusions and protocol limits. Out: complete field-bound validation/decorators (US-002), database columns and read mapping (US-003), route/provider policy (US-004), capability enforcement and token minting (US-005), result parsing (US-006), runner and web behavior (US-007–011).

**Interface** — `normalizeDispatch(dto, defaultBranch)` returns `agentInput: AgentJobInput | null` (non-null only for `AGENT`). `NewFleetJob` gains optional `agentInput?: AgentJobInput | null`.
```typescript
AgentAssign { name: string; task: string; model?: string; modelAliases?: Record<string, string>; timeoutSec?: number }
```
The result shape is `AgentJobResult { status, model?, output, truncated, deniedAsks, deniedAsksTruncated, costUsd? }`, where status is completed|failed|cancelled|timeout, denied asks are approval {kind,tool,summary} or question {kind,text}, and fitted costUsd is an optional decimal string. `AGENT_NAME_RE` is `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$`. `AGENT_RESULT_LIMITS = { budgetBytes: 12288, maxOutputBytes: 8192, maxDeniedAsks: 10, maxAskChars: 500, maxToolChars: 128, maxModelChars: 200 }`, re-exported from the protocol index. Write failing cases in dispatch-input.spec.ts, dispatch-fleet-job.dto.spec.ts and protocol.spec.ts before implementation.

userStories.title: Agent input bounds
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enforce every agent input bound in service-level normalization and mirror those constraints in DispatchAgentDto.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, section Steps) runs every judgment step (spec review, PRD review, finding classification) as an `AGENT` job that runs `nax agents run` with the flow's reviewer role.

**Approach** — Verbatim design: **Bounds, all in `normalizeDispatch`.** `name` matches `AGENT_NAME_RE` `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$` (a nax catalog name, plugin-qualified names included) and contains no `..`; `task` is 1-16,384 characters and not only whitespace (nax refuses an empty task); `model` is 1-200 non-whitespace characters; `modelAliases` holds at most 8 entries, keys match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`, and every value has nax's alias-target shape (`provider/model` or `acp:<claude|codex|cursor>[/<model>]`, optional `[effort]`, no whitespace), copied from nax `config/schemas-model-alias.ts` so a bad value fails at dispatch instead of failing nax's config load on the runner; `timeoutSec` is an integer 60-86,400. `normalizeDispatch` enforces every bound, because F3 calls the service with a DTO it builds itself and no validation pipe; `DispatchAgentDto` carries the same bounds as decorators for the OpenAPI document and the HTTP route. koda does not check that the agent or model exists: only the runner's catalog knows, and nax reports an unknown one as an error that fails the job.

Add bound constants and isModelAliasTarget to US-001's local agent-jobs module. Reject malformed agent objects/field types rather than trusting a TypeScript DTO instance; preserve accepted task/model/alias values, including slash-prefixed skill tasks, rather than rewriting them. Every failure uses ValidationAppException and fleet.dispatchInput with exact reason agent.name, agent.task, agent.model, agent.modelAliases or agent.timeoutSec.

**Scope** — In: all normalization field checks, alias grammar and matching nested DTO validators/Swagger bounds. Out: persistence guards (US-003), GitHub/provider/permission enforcement (US-004), runner assign re-validation (US-007), and runner profile aliases (US-008). No server-side catalog/model existence check.

**Interface** — `normalizeDispatch(dto, defaultBranch)`; `DispatchAgentDto`; `AGENT_NAME_RE`; `isModelAliasTarget`. Input remains `agent: { name, task, model?, modelAliases?, timeoutSec? }`. Extend dispatch-input.spec.ts and dispatch-fleet-job.dto.spec.ts with table-driven rejection/boundary cases before implementation; tests must call normalizeDispatch directly as well as validate nested DTOs.

userStories.title: AGENT job persistence
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist immutable agent input and mutable per-attempt results, exposing them on FleetJobDto and clearing only results on requeue.

**Motivation** — koda has no job that runs an arbitrary agent task and returns its text: `REVIEW` and `FIX` post to a PR, `PLAN` and `RUN` produce a PRD or a branch, and config jobs run no agent.

**Approach** — Verbatim story design: New nullable JSON columns `FleetJob.agentInput` and `FleetJob.agentResult` (migration `20261127090000_fleet_job_agent`), mapped through guards, written on insert, patched by the mirror, cleared on requeue (`agentResult` only) and exposed on `FleetJobDto` as `agent` and `agentResult`.

Verbatim integration target: `NewFleetJob` gains optional `agentInput?: AgentJobInput | null`; `FleetJobRecord` gains optional `agentInput?: AgentJobInput | null` and `agentResult?: AgentJobResult | null` (the `fixOutcome?` precedent, so the typed record fixtures in existing specs keep compiling); `toJob` always sets both, null when absent; `agentResult` joins the patch keys.

Insert writes agentInput as SQL null when absent; patch writing handles agentResult null as Prisma.DbNull. Map both JSON columns through shape guards rather than unchecked assertions. FleetJobDto.from maps agentInput to agent and agentResult with ?? null, preserving existing envelope/detail behavior. Requeue adds agentResult:null to its existing reset patch without clearing input or altering epoch/cost bookkeeping. Apply the migration over the preceding schema and verify existing rows remain null, using the scratch-schema migration helper pattern. US-006 does not exist yet: do not import its future parser; use local persistence guards that can be reused later.

**Scope** — In: Prisma columns/migration, optional domain fields, insert/read/patch guards, public DTO mapping and requeue reset. Out: dispatch service wiring/provider policy (US-004), runner assignment/token policy (US-005), full untrusted snapshot bounds/parser (US-006). Do not change the active-job unique index.

**Interface** — `FleetJob.agentInput Json?`; `FleetJob.agentResult Json?`; `FleetJobPatch` includes agentResult. `FleetJobDto` gains `agent` and `agentResult`; `from` maps them with `?? null`. Write repository/DTO guard tests and real PostgreSQL round-trip/requeue/migration tests as part of implementation. Use canRunDbTests and actually execute DB suites outside the sandbox; regenerate the Prisma client after schema changes.

userStories.title: AGENT through the dispatch route
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Dispatch authorized GitHub AGENT jobs through the existing route/service, include them in budget hard stops and publish the generated API contract.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, section Steps) runs every judgment step (spec review, PRD review, finding classification) as an `AGENT` job that runs `nax agents run` with the flow's reviewer role.

**Approach** — Verbatim design: **GitHub only.** The read-only guarantee needs a read-only forge token, which only GitHub mints (the broker refuses any read-only or purpose request on GitLab rather than fall back to the write-capable stored token). `AGENT` on a GitLab repo is refused at dispatch with 422 `agent is GitHub-only`, as `REVIEW` and `FIX` are.

**No bundle ingest, no analytics.** The runner still uploads its usual bundle; ingest's eligibility rule does not name `AGENT`, so it is not ingested. Fleet analytics (`NAX_JOBS`, `RUN`/`PLAN`) and the assistant's dispatch tool are unchanged. `AGENT` joins the budget hard stop list, so a paused scope cancels queued `AGENT` jobs.

Verbatim cost design: `nax agents run` has no cost cap. `maxCostUsd` stays required on the dispatch body and is stored, but it is not enforced for `AGENT`; the job reports `costUsd` when nax priced the run. A flow checks its cap between jobs (F3).

Extend the existing provider exception without changing REVIEW/FIX messages. Store normalizeDispatch's agentInput via the existing transactional insert. Keep ProjectMembershipGuard/RequiresGuard, fleet.job.dispatch, approval route gating, actor/audit attribution, live publication after commit and immediate placement behavior unchanged. A duplicate active repo/feature still returns 409 with activeJobId. Add AGENT to BUDGET_STOP_COMMANDS. The endpoint still returns the existing JsonResponse envelope containing DispatchResultDto.job; do not replace it with a flat DTO. Add endpoint e2e and OpenAPI contract cases, then run bun run generate from repository root to regenerate openapi.json and the CLI client, never editing generated files manually.

**Scope** — In: route/service AGENT support, GitLab rejection, permission and existing REVIEW/FIX provider-policy regression, budget hard stop, endpoint tests, and regenerated openapi.json plus the generated CLI client artifacts. Out: token minting/placement support (US-005), result sync (US-006), runner execution (US-007–010), web labels/panel (US-011). No web/assistant/hand-written CLI AGENT dispatch and no AGENT analytics/ingest.

**Interface** — `FleetJobsService.dispatch(actorId, projectId, dto, opts)`; `POST /api/projects/:slug/fleet/jobs` under `fleet.job.dispatch`; public `agent` and `agentResult` from US-003. Use strict isolated tests for route authorization/provider restrictions and real DB endpoint/budget behavior; ensure the queued dispatch fixture has no fitting runner.

userStories.title: Placement, assign and read-only token for AGENT
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Place AGENT only on capable runners, serialize its input and grant a separately cached read-only GitHub default-repo token.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, section Steps) runs every judgment step (spec review, PRD review, finding classification) as an `AGENT` job that runs `nax agents run` with the flow's reviewer role.

**Approach** — Verbatim design: **Read-only token.** The broker gains `purpose: 'read'`: GitHub only, cache key `<jobId>:<leaseEpoch>:read`, minted with `mintReadOnlyToken`, and returned without `repoId`, so the runner's token cache matches it to the job's default token request. The default-repo grant in `SyncService` passes `purpose: 'read'` for `AGENT`. The runner adds no publish step.

Verbatim capability rule: A runner without it gets misfit `agents_run`, which is recoverable (not in `PERMANENT_MISFITS`): a runner upgrade fixes it.

Add agentsRun to the server's capability validator as true-or-absent (false is an error with field agentsRun), add agents_run to MisfitReason, dashboard reason list and PlacementMisfitDto enum, and build agent only for AGENT from FleetJobRecord.agentInput with no review block. Preserve all other placement constraints and allow a pinned missing-capability job to queue. No eligible agentsRun runner means QUEUED, not terminal failure. Extend GitTokenBroker.mint/fresh purpose types, read-only mint branch and independent read cache key; preserve default RUN/write, REVIEW/FIX and PROJECT repo-scoped readOnly semantics. Reject a GitLab read purpose as provider_error before cache/token lookup, never falling back to stored write credentials. Distinguish purpose read from readOnly:true: the latter is the existing PROJECT grant WITH repoId, while AGENT must have NO repoId. SyncService grants read only on the job's default repository request after existing runner/lease/state fencing and mints outside transactions.

**Scope** — In: capability validation, recoverable placement misfit, assign serialization, read-purpose mint/cache isolation and sync grant. Out: capability probing/runner parser/token-cache regression (US-007), spawning/no-publish execution (US-008–010), result mirroring (US-006), dispatch provider policy (US-004). No GitLab fallback or credential logging/persistence.

**Interface** — `GitTokenBroker.mint(req)` changes `purpose?: 'review' | 'fix'` to `purpose?: 'review' | 'fix' | 'read'`; `fresh` accepts the same purposes. `RunnerCapabilities.agentsRun?: true`; `MisfitReason` includes 'agents_run'; `buildAssignPayload` adds `agent` for AGENT. Follow git-token.broker.purpose.spec.ts, capabilities.spec.ts, placement-rules.spec.ts, assign-payload.spec.ts and sync.service.token-purpose.spec.ts, with held-job sync integration cases. Use strict three-session TDD for token/cache/authorization isolation.

userStories.title: AGENT result mirror
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Validate bounded untrusted agent results and persist valid snapshot fields without rejecting unrelated fields or the sync.

**Motivation** — koda has no job that runs an arbitrary agent task and returns its text: `REVIEW` and `FIX` post to a PR, `PLAN` and `RUN` produce a PRD or a branch, and config jobs run no agent.

**Approach** — Verbatim result contract: nax prints one JSON object on stdout: `{ agent, model, status, output, deniedAsks, costUsd? }`. The runner reads at most 16 MiB of `nax.stdout` (`AGENT_STDOUT_MAX_BYTES`), turns the object into `AgentJobResult { status, model?, output, truncated, deniedAsks, deniedAsksTruncated, costUsd? }` and sends it as the snapshot field `agentResult`. A sync event payload is at most 16,384 bytes, so the result has a serialized budget of 12,288 bytes (the config-job precedent): `AGENT_RESULT_LIMITS = { budgetBytes: 12288, maxOutputBytes: 8192, maxDeniedAsks: 10, maxAskChars: 500, maxToolChars: 128, maxModelChars: 200 }`.

Verbatim API behavior: koda checks the same limits (its own copy, pinned equal to the protocol's; the API's `AgentJobInput` and `AgentJobResult` types are structural mirrors of the protocol's, as `config-jobs` is) and drops the result whole when any fails (the `configResult` precedent).

Add the runtime limits to the API's existing local agent-jobs module, pinned to protocol values in protocol.spec.ts (runtime package imports in production remain forbidden). Implement parseAgentResult in sync/agent-result.ts: reject non-object values, unsupported statuses, wrong types/discriminants/booleans, oversized model/output/asks and serialized byte budget, and invalid optional cost strings; return a clean structural result, retaining omission of costUsd. Status is completed|failed|cancelled|timeout; asks are {kind:'approval',tool,summary} or {kind:'question',text}. Cost has the existing nonnegative decimal-string shape, at most four fractional digits. mirror calls this parser for agentResult and only includes a valid parsed field in FleetJobPatch, keeping other snapshot fields intact. The existing fenced report processor and US-003 patch writer perform persistence and DTO exposure.

**Scope** — In: local runtime result limits, parseAgentResult, snapshot mirror and held-job sync round-trip. Out: DB columns/patch implementation (US-003), runner reading/fitting (US-009), terminal verdicts (US-010), result display (US-011). Do not repair/truncate malformed results on the server or make a bad result fatal to sync.

**Interface** — `AgentJobResult { status, model?, output, truncated, deniedAsks, deniedAsksTruncated, costUsd? }`; `parseAgentResult` returns a parsed AgentJobResult or null. `interpretEvent('snapshot', ...)` returns `{ kind:'mirror', patch }`; result assertions read `effect.patch`, and an invalid agentResult key is omitted only from that patch, not treated as an invalid whole event. Use table-driven unit tests plus real held-AGENT sync/GET integration tests, reusing config-result/event-payload precedents and the DB gate.

**Goal** — Spawn detached nax agents run with a private task file, per-job model aliases and an explicit timeout using the existing job environment.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, section Steps) runs every judgment step (spec review, PRD review, finding classification) as an `AGENT` job that runs `nax agents run` with the flow's reviewer role.

**Approach** — Verbatim design: **Task on a file.** The runner writes the task to `agent-task.md` in the job directory (mode 0600) and passes `--task-file`, so the task never meets argv limits or shows in the process list. The file is an attempt file (a new attempt starts without it) and `cleanup` deletes it. A task starting with `/<name>` is expanded by nax as a skill invocation; F3 relies on this for `/spec-review`.

Verbatim timeout design: The runner always passes `--timeout`: `timeoutSec` when set, else 3,600 seconds (`AGENT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SEC`, nax's own default turn limit), so a run is always bounded.

Verbatim argv approach, with `chain = [...profiles, 'koda-job-<jobId>'].join(',')`:
```text
[...naxCommand, 'agents', 'run', <name>, '--task-file', <jobDir>/agent-task.md, '--json', '--profile', <chain>,

```
It runs in the clone directory, as every nax job does, with the same environment `HostExecutor.spawn` builds (provider key socket included). The per-job profile carries `agent.modelAliases` when the job has aliases, so a flow can pass `model: 'reviewer'` with `modelAliases: { reviewer: 'acp:claude' }`.

userStories.title: AGENT result reader
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Read nax's bounded JSON stdout and fit its typed result into the protocol's serialized snapshot budget with a preserved output tail.

**Motivation** — nax 0.91.8-canary.4 ships `nax agents run` (unattended, denies asks, prints a JSON result), and the koda runner now uses that version, so the job kind can be built.

**Approach** — Verbatim design: **Result.** nax prints one JSON object on stdout: `{ agent, model, status, output, deniedAsks, costUsd? }`. The runner reads at most 16 MiB of `nax.stdout` (`AGENT_STDOUT_MAX_BYTES`), turns the object into `AgentJobResult { status, model?, output, truncated, deniedAsks, deniedAsksTruncated, costUsd? }` and sends it as the snapshot field `agentResult`. A sync event payload is at most 16,384 bytes, so the result has a serialized budget of 12,288 bytes (the config-job precedent): `AGENT_RESULT_LIMITS = { budgetBytes: 12288, maxOutputBytes: 8192, maxDeniedAsks: 10, maxAskChars: 500, maxToolChars: 128, maxModelChars: 200 }`. `fitAgentResult` cuts `model` to 200 characters, keeps the first 10 denied asks with `text` and `summary` cut to 500 and `tool` to 128 characters, keeps the last 8,192 UTF-8 bytes of `output` (the flow's verdict JSON sits at the end, F4), then drops denied asks from the end and then shortens the output tail further until `JSON.stringify(result)` fits the budget, setting `truncated` and `deniedAsksTruncated` when it cut. The whole stdout is in the job log. koda checks the same limits (its own copy, pinned equal to the protocol's; the API's `AgentJobInput` and `AgentJobResult` types are structural mirrors of the protocol's, as `config-jobs` is) and drops the result whole when any fails (the `configResult` precedent).

Verbatim nax contract: With `--json`, stdout is one JSON object `{ agent, model, status: 'completed' | 'failed' | 'cancelled' | 'timeout', output, deniedAsks: [{ kind: 'approval', tool, summary } | { kind: 'question', text }], costUsd? }`; `costUsd` is omitted when unpriced.

Implement readAgentResult(jobDir) with a bounded stdout read and typed field validation before returning a raw parsed result (cost numeric when present). Empty/malformed JSON, unsupported shape/status, missing files or stdout over the limit return ok:false, with the first non-empty nax.stderr line cut to 300 characters when one exists. Do not infer result status from process exit code; usage/config/trust/catalog failures may produce only stderr. fitAgentResult uses protocol runtime limits and formatCost for optional decimal-string cost; omission is retained for unpriced runs. Measure serialized JSON in UTF-8 bytes, account for escaping, and never split UTF-8 characters when retaining the tail. Unlike fitConfigResult's reduction order, AGENT drops asks before shortening the already-bounded output tail. Full stdout/stderr remain available to the normal log/bundle paths.

**Scope** — In: bounded result reader, stderr fallback, tail fitting/truncation flags and optional cost formatting. Out: final JobRun verdict/snapshot (US-010), API result validation/persistence (US-006) and result UI (US-011). No flow verdict-JSON parsing, partial-result streaming, output redaction or enlargement of the 8,192-byte result tail.

**Interface** — `readAgentResult(jobDir)` returns `{ ok:true }` with the parsed nax result or `{ ok:false, stderrLine? }`; `fitAgentResult` produces AgentJobResult; `AGENT_STDOUT_MAX_BYTES` is 16 MiB. `AgentJobResult { status, model?, output, truncated, deniedAsks, deniedAsksTruncated, costUsd? }`. Use real temporary stdout/stderr files and table-driven tests for malformed data, size/field boundaries, escaping and cost; reuse tailBytes/formatCost behavior, not the config-result trimming order.

userStories.title: AGENT verdict
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Judge AGENT from its final parsed result and cancellation request, reporting the fitted result and optional cost once through the existing finish lifecycle.

**Motivation** — koda has no job that runs an arbitrary agent task and returns its text: `REVIEW` and `FIX` post to a PR, `PLAN` and `RUN` produce a PRD or a branch, and config jobs run no agent.

**Approach** — Verbatim design: **Verdict.** Cancel requested: `CANCELLED`. Otherwise status `completed`: `COMPLETED`; status `failed`, `timeout` or `cancelled`: `FAILED` with reason `agent <status>`; no parseable result: `FAILED` with reason `agent result unreadable` plus `: ` and the first non-empty line of `nax.stderr` (at most 300 characters) when there is one. The job's `costSpentUsd` is the result's `costUsd` formatted by the runner's `formatCost`.

Verbatim bundle constraint: The runner still uploads its usual bundle; ingest's eligibility rule does not name `AGENT`, so it is not ingested.

Add an AGENT branch to JobRun.judge using US-009's readAgentResult/fitAgentResult. A readable result populates snapshot.agentResult; a priced result also populates snapshot.costSpentUsd from the fitted four-place string, while unknown cost adds no costSpentUsd. An unreadable result adds no agentResult. Cancel wins over nax status and unreadable-result failures. workflow is undefined for AGENT. Preserve finish's log drain, RUNNING->UPLOADING->terminal transitions, bundle retry/fencing behavior and journal-before-send ordering; the existing finish sends the judged snapshot after upload, then the terminal state. Do not enter RUN status/workflow/finish-ledger/progress-push or PLAN commit paths and do not add publication. Results are reported once at the end, not each watch tick; restart finish uses the same judgment.
